task.description:
WF-03 Step 2 (fix design) for ISS-0703, on branch feature/WF03-ISS0703-20260917 (already checked out and pushed -- `git checkout feature/WF03-ISS0703-20260917` if your session starts elsewhere). Read ISSUE-FIXER's full diagnosis at handoffs/WF03-ISS0703-20260917/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnosis.json's result.summary in full -- do not re-derive the diagnosis, it is already done. Root cause: Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier.Oidcc.verify_bearer_token/2 (lib/letflow/oidc/token_verifier/oidcc.ex:30-45) lets an exception raised deep inside the oidcc/jose dependency chain (a CaseClauseError from jose_base64url.decode!/2, triggered when the raw bearer token is not valid base64url/JWT-shaped -- e.g. garbage or non-token input) propagate uncaught, through Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline.verify_token/1 (auth_pipeline.ex:245-254, which only pattern-matches {:ok,_}/{:error,_} tuples, not exceptions), all the way to a raw Bandit HTTP 500 with an empty body -- instead of the auth pipeline's documented design intent that every verifier {:error,_reason} collapses to a single well-formed 401 Problem+JSON response (see auth_pipeline.ex's own comments around lines 241-254). The module's own moduledoc (oidcc.ex lines 20-27) falsely claims it 'never raises' -- that claim does not hold for malformed/non-JWT-shaped input.

Design a fix: verify_bearer_token/2 must catch any exception raised by Oidcc.Token.validate_jwt/3 (and defensively Oidcc.ClientContext.from_configuration_worker/4, the other oidcc call in this function) and convert it into an {:error, reason} tuple that Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline.verify_token/1's existing error-collapse path already knows how to turn into a 401 -- so no change should be needed to auth_pipeline.ex itself unless your design finds a real gap there. Choose an appropriate rescue/catch shape (a `try`/`rescue`, or `Kernel.catch`-and-classify style already used elsewhere in this codebase if a convention exists -- check lib/letflow/oidc/ and lib/letflow/plugs/ for precedent before inventing a new shape) and a specific {:error, reason} tag that fits the existing error-tuple vocabulary this module/pipeline already uses (read verify_bearer_token/2's existing {:error, ...} return shapes and match the convention, do not invent an inconsistent new atom). Also design the moduledoc correction: the 'never raises' claim must be fixed to state accurately what is now guaranteed (never raises; malformed/invalid input, including non-base64url/non-JWT-shaped tokens, now returns {:error, ...}).

This is a design document only -- no implementation code, per this project's design/implementation split (see CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own gate criteria). State exact function signatures/specs, the exact {:error, reason} shape, and where the rescue boundary sits, precisely enough that ELIXIR-DEV and TEST-DESIGNER need no further judgement calls. Write the design artefact to lib/letflow/design/iss0703-oidc-verifier-exception-handling.md (standard location, see docs/agents/AGENT_SYSTEM.md for the convention).

REWORK ITERATION 1: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAILED the first version of this design (see handoffs/WF03-ISS0703-20260917/step-02b-code-design-validator.json's result for the full verdict) on AC5 (no implementation code) only -- every other acceptance criterion passed. Two specific, named gaps to fix, nothing else in the design needs to change: (1) Section 4 contains a literal, complete, pasteable Elixir statement (a Logger.warning/1 call with real string interpolation) -- replace it with a description of what gets logged (the fields/shape), not a literal statement. (2) Section 5 renders a full `def ... rescue ... catch ... end` skeleton in real Elixir syntax beyond its legitimate @spec/def-head signature -- the validator noted Section 2's prose already conveys the same clause-placement information without a code block, so remove the fenced code skeleton from Section 5 and keep only the signature/spec plus prose description of clause placement; do not remove any substantive content, only the fenced implementation-shaped block. (Section 3's fenced block, an unmodified quote of EXISTING auth_pipeline.ex code offered as evidence, was confirmed fine and does not need to change.) Finish this handoff normally: flip status to COMPLETED and result.status to PASS/FAIL as usual when you're done -- this is not a first dispatch, so do not re-read this as an instruction to merely set IN_PROGRESS and stop.
acceptance_criteria: Design states the exact rescue/catch boundary (which call(s) it wraps) and the exact {:error, reason} tuple shape returned on a caught exception, consistent with verify_bearer_token/2's existing error vocabulary
Design covers both Oidcc.Token.validate_jwt/3 and Oidcc.ClientContext.from_configuration_worker/4 (or explicitly justifies excluding the latter if it cannot raise on malformed input)
Design states the corrected moduledoc text (accurate 'never raises' claim)

Design states what TEST-DESIGNER's regression test must exercise: the REAL Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier.Oidcc adapter (not TokenVerifierDouble) with a non-JWT-shaped Authorization/bearer-token value, proving fail-then-pass
No .ex implementation code bodies in the design doc -- signatures/specs/shapes only
No changes proposed to auth_pipeline.ex's error-collapse logic unless the design identifies a real, specific gap there (state explicitly if none found)

result.summary: REWORK ITERATION 1: fixed the two AC5 gaps CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR named in handoffs/WF03-ISS0703-20260917/step-02b-code-design-validator.json (FAIL), without altering any other substance. (1) Section 4: removed the literal, pasteable `Logger.warning("...")` statement with real string interpolation; replaced with prose describing the log message's content (names module+function, then the same kind/message fields placed in the returned tuple) without presenting it as executable code. (2) Section 5: removed the fenced `def ... rescue ... catch ... end` skeleton written in real Elixir syntax; kept only the legitimate @impl/@spec/def-head signature block, and replaced the removed skeleton with a prose paragraph restating clause placement (with-expression stays the def body; rescue and catch clauses appended per §2; each branch's kind/message construction per §3/§4) -- Section 2's existing prose already carried this information, so nothing substantive was lost. Section 3's fenced block (an unmodified quote of existing auth_pipeline.ex code, confirmed fine by the validator) was left untouched. No other section was changed: rescue/catch boundary scope (both oidcc calls, one boundary), error-tuple shape ({:verifier_crashed, %{kind, message}}), the AC6 finding of no auth_pipeline.ex gap, the moduledoc correction text, and the AC4 TEST-DESIGNER guidance (real Oidcc adapter, unit + integration, fail-then-pass) are all unchanged from the prior PASS-on-5-of-6 version. Verified via grep that only two fenced code blocks now remain beyond the removed ones: the @type shape in Section 3 and the auth_pipeline.ex quote in Section 3, plus the @spec/def-head in Section 5 -- all legitimate per WF-02 Step 1b check 2e/2b.
